why_it_exists: Every source needs one safe, repeatable way in, so a failing or missing source never stops the product.
input: Source credentials; connector settings; schedules; inbound webhooks
processing: One reusable connector per source: key from secrets, rate limits, retries (429, 500, 504 with exponential backoff and jitter; 400, 401, 403 never retried), re-authentication where tokens expire (ZoomInfo JWT about 60 minutes), source and date stamp, write to memory. Scheduler for daily runs; webhook intake for push events; cached mode when a key is missing
output: Records in memory with source and date; run logs; events
in_r1: Framework; data providers; signal sources; three CRMs (read); email and calendar; webhook intake
in_r2: Marketing, analytics, call and conversation connectors by configuration
if_it_fails: Retry, then last good data marked stale and an admin alert; no key: cached mode

why_it_exists: The same person appears in the CRM, email, LinkedIn and data providers. Without one record, signals and sends attach to the wrong person.
input: Contact and account records from every source
processing: One record per person and per account. Match on LinkedIn URL, then email, then name + company + title. LinkedIn URL is the tiebreaker: same name, company and title with a different URL are two people. Source kept on every field. Bounces and job changes mark a contact stale
output: One resolved record with an identity tier I1 to I5 (section 6)
if_it_fails: A disputed record (I4) is held, retried each refresh, and goes to the rep or admin after three failed cycles

why_it_exists: Every agent must read the same history before it acts and write back after. This memory is what compounds, and it is what the customer owns.
processing: Single memory every agent reads before acting and writes after every outcome. Entities: people, accounts, deals, signals, actions, reasons, outcomes, documents. Linked person to account to deal and signal to action to reason to outcome. Tenant isolation. Readable and editable by the client team
output: The memory core and the account dossier passed down the pipeline
in_r1: Full schema for R1 entities; client read and edit of ICP, exclusions, contacts, personas (audited)
in_r2: Edit of the remaining objects; corpus, warm path and review tables
in_r3: Learning tables (weights, edits, objections, patterns, quota)
if_it_fails: A failed migration rolls back; the store goes read only until fixed

why_it_exists: A signal that is months old must stop counting, or old news keeps ranking accounts.
input: Every signal and time bound fact
processing: Expiry set at capture from the tier window; a date in the source overrides it ("budget frozen to April" expires in April). Nightly job marks expired facts; scoring ignores them
output: An expiry on every signal; expired facts excluded
in_r1: Tier windows; nightly expiry; dates from content
if_it_fails: A fact with no usable window is not written

why_it_exists: Contacting a customer, a competitor or someone who opted out is the costliest mistake, so this check comes before everything else.
input: CRM customers, open deals, competitors, partners, paused segments, recent touches, do-not-contact, opt-outs
processing: One list with reason, source and date. Checked before segmentation, before any recommendation and before any send. Suppression is its contact-level part (opted out, wrong person, do not contact)
output: A pass or a hold with the reason
in_r1: CRM read plus manual upload and manual suppression
in_r2: Opt-outs added automatically from reply statuses
if_it_fails: If the list cannot be read the action is held and goes to the owning rep

why_it_exists: A rep, and the AI, must see one account's whole story from first touch to today.
input: Signals, actions, decisions, sends, replies, outcomes
processing: Ordered view from first touch to today with links to each source row
in_r1: Signals, actions, decisions, sends, replies, outcomes
if_it_fails: A missing source is shown as a gap

why_it_exists: Any rank or action must be explainable later, with the evidence and the rules in force that day.
input: Every rank, approval, edit, hold, escalation
processing: Append-only row per decision with actor, evidence, and the version of thresholds, tiers, prompts and cache state in force, so a March decision is explainable in June
in_r1: Every rank, route, approval, edit, hold
if_it_fails: If the write fails the action is blocked (nothing happens unlogged)

why_it_exists: Outcomes only teach the system if every send is logged with its exact cause.
input: An action at the moment it is sent
processing: Records person, segment, signal ids, message version, rule version and channel so outcomes join the exact cause
if_it_fails: A send outside the system is rebuilt from the approval and flagged "late capture"

why_it_exists: Messages and assets must be grounded in the customer's own documents and cite them, so nothing is invented.
input: Datasheets, case studies, decks, proof points, brand templates, client documents
processing: Upload, tag, quality check, chunk, embed and index. Retrieval with citations (RAG): every claim in a draft or asset links to the page it came from. Per client; never shared across clients
output: A searchable, quality-checked library with citations
in_r2: Quality checks; backlog of unanswered questions
if_it_fails: No relevant document: no claim is made from it; the question goes to the content backlog

why_it_exists: Reps should ask, decide and act in one conversation, not across screens.
processing: Orchestrator routes each question to the right agent and returns a card: ranked list, cited answer, draft, escalation. History, roles, escalation queue
output: One conversation for asking, deciding and approving
in_r2: Slack and Teams interactive bots; CLI
if_it_fails: Unrecognised question: ask to rephrase with examples; an agent failure is stated with the last good data

why_it_exists: Nothing should reach reps until it has been tested on cases where the answer is already known.
input: 45 known accounts (15 won, 15 lost, 15 random); golden sets; hand-labelled replies
processing: Run blind, compare, pass or fix, dry run, go live, monitor. Nothing reaches reps until it passes. Bars are suggested defaults agreed per client (section 9)
output: A pass or fail report; release blocked on fail
in_r2: Reply classifier bar (90% weighted, zero missed opt-outs); plays and drafts bars
in_r3: Repeated on every rule or prompt change
if_it_fails: No client history: use the customer's CRM wins and losses or a peer set and mark the result provisional

feature: Versioned prompts, rules and cost logging
why_it_exists: Prompts and rules change. Every change must be versioned, costed and reversible.
input: Every prompt, rule, tier table and model call
processing: Prompts and thresholds are versioned and tracked by acceptance rate; cost per call, per run and per account logged; caps and alerts
output: A version and a cost on every call
in_r3: Small tuned models for repeat work
if_it_fails: A failed cost log raises an alert; the call proceeds

why_it_exists: Lessons from lost deals and objections must be stored so the system can use them later.
processing: Stores lost-deal lessons, winning replies per objection, edits per segment
output: Lessons and winning replies per segment
in_r2: Capture: reasons from Disqualified replies and edits

why_it_exists: When the AI cannot decide, a named person must get the item with a reason, a deadline and a default.
processing: The AI decides what it can. What it cannot (medium confidence, cache miss, disputed identity, name-only CRM match, unsure reply, unreadable protective check) goes to the owning sales rep; campaign-level items go to the sales manager; configuration items go to the admin. Each item has an owner, a reason, a due time and a default if nobody acts
output: A queue with owner, reason, due time, default
in_r1: Rep queue; manager and admin items; defaults on timeout
in_r3: Fewer escalations as confidence is calibrated
if_it_fails: If nobody acts by the due time the default applies: individual NBAs instead of an NBC, expire a draft, keep a record held

why_it_exists: Each customer needs its own setup. Reaching a first ranked queue in four weeks depends on setup being configuration, not code.
input: The customer's ICP, CRM, closed-won field, tier table, thresholds, brand, autonomy policy
processing: Per-customer configuration, never a shared pool. Cold start in four weeks: connect CRM and data providers; load won and lost deals and draft the scoring rules; backtest; first ranked queue
in_r1: Configuration, cold start, ontology pack per vertical
if_it_fails: Missing configuration blocks go-live with a named gap

why_it_exists: Different people need different access, and one customer's data must never mix with another's.
processing: Roles: sales rep, sales manager, sales leader, admin. Territory-based access. tenant_id on every row. Append-only audit of configuration and access changes
output: Access decisions and an audit log

why_it_exists: The customer may or may not know their ICP. Either way a confirmed ICP is needed to start.
input: Either the ICP the customer shares (typed in chat, a form or a document), or, if they are unsure, their website and a short interview; past won accounts where the CRM has them
processing: Two paths into one confirmed ICP. Path A, the customer shares an ICP: it is parsed into criteria and weights and shown back to confirm. Path B, the customer does not know their ICP: the AI reads their website (products, industries served, case studies) and, where useful, runs a short interview, then proposes a draft ICP with a sample of matching accounts; the admin edits and confirms. Either way the confirmed ICP is versioned and the list is built from it
output: A confirmed, versioned ICP filter per customer
in_r1: ICP shared, or proposed from the website and an interview; confirm and edit
if_it_fails: Website unreadable or interview unfinished: ask for the ICP in a form

why_it_exists: The confirmed ICP must turn into a list of real candidate accounts and contacts.
processing: Provider queries by the ICP criteria (industry, size, region, titles); returns candidate accounts and contacts with free attributes only (firmographics, titles), so fit can be checked before any paid call
if_it_fails: One provider down: the next; all down: cached list flagged

why_it_exists: No single data provider is complete. Trying the cheapest first controls cost.
processing: Apollo first (broadest, cheapest), then ZoomInfo, then Lusha (last resort, fills mobile gaps). A provider that returns empty triggers the next. Apollo first-try hits are accepted; ZoomInfo fallback hits are cross-checked against Lusha
output: Raw records tagged by provider and how they were found
if_it_fails: All providers fail: hold, retry next cycle, then escalate

why_it_exists: Providers can disagree. Each record needs a trust level so doubtful ones are not used blindly.
processing: Assign an identity tier from how the record was found (section 6); carry the tier into scoring
output: An identity-resolved record with tier I1 to I5
if_it_fails: I4 held; I3 proceeds as unconfirmed

why_it_exists: Only accounts that fit should be paid for, so fit is judged on free attributes first.
processing: Score each candidate against the ICP on the free attributes, weighting each criterion by how strongly the category research shows it correlates with buying. Only candidates that pass go on to paid enrichment: this is the cost rule, pay for data only when an account fits
in_r1: Default weights; research weights where available

why_it_exists: The list must not contain existing customers or open deals.
input: The list; read access to the customer's CRM
processing: Read closed-won from the customer's field and value. Domain match on both sides: exclude with confidence. Name-only match: hold, do not drop silently. Link a person to a CRM contact at 70 confidence or more on a genuine identifying match. Read-only
output: A clean list; customers removed; name-only matches held
if_it_fails: CRM unreachable: nothing passes to outreach until the check runs

why_it_exists: Reps need verified contact details and company facts, paid for only when an account fits.
processing: Firmographics, name, title, LinkedIn at match; verified email and phone only when triggered; domain and title cross-check; trust the provider's verification. ZoomInfo: one credit per record, then Under Management for 12 months at no further credit
if_it_fails: A contradiction is flagged, not accepted; an I4 record never arrives here

why_it_exists: The next stages need the whole list and everything collected, not a summary.
input: The enriched list with identity tiers
processing: The whole list and every collected field pass on, with no export and no second tool

why_it_exists: Doubtful records must not vanish or pass silently. They are held, retried, then given to a person.
input: Records held at identity, CRM match or profile change
processing: Retry on each refresh; after three failed cycles escalate to the rep or admin to resolve the dispute, confirm the match or accept the change. I3 is not escalated

why_it_exists: People change jobs and emails. Stored records must stay right without good data being overwritten by errors.
input: A record whose email, company or LinkedIn URL differs from what is stored
processing: Scheduled re-run. Change under 30 days old: cross-verify with one more provider, accept if it agrees, otherwise hold. Over 30 days: accept and log. Updates our record only; the customer's CRM is never written to
output: A reconciled record; a change log

why_it_exists: The team must see where data coverage is thin so the waterfall can be widened.
input: Provider results per channel and customer
processing: Measures coverage (strong on LinkedIn, thin on email) and tells the waterfall which provider tier to expand next. Thin coverage is not evidence that no signal exists

why_it_exists: Every signal type needs a defined source, level, tier and window in one place.
input: The list of signals, sources, levels, tiers
processing: Configurable registry: signal, level, source or API, capture method, tier, window, release. New signals start at the tier default

why_it_exists: Signals must be fetched for each target account on a schedule.
input: Accounts on the list; named sources
processing: For each account query the named sources on schedule; a match becomes a timestamped signal; a non-match is discarded
in_r1: Pull on schedule; push events from competitor sources reconciled
if_it_fails: Source down: last good run, stale

why_it_exists: A whole sector moving (rules, energy, news) changes timing for many accounts at once.
processing: Industry and regulatory events, energy and commodity shifts, narrative news and trends (GDELT, Firecrawl monitor, NewsCatcher, Exa Monitors, regulatory calendars)

why_it_exists: Events at an account (tenders, funding, hiring) are the clearest evidence of timing.
processing: Tenders and plant expansions, capex, funding, hiring surges, new plant heads, M&A, filing language, tech-stack changes, breach or incident, patents (Crunchbase, PredictLeads, SEC EDGAR, BuiltWith, Apollo job postings, tender portals)
if_it_fails: Licence missing: cached then seeded and labelled

why_it_exists: An account committed to a rival, or one that is weakening, is a reason to act now.
processing: Contract renewal with a rival, declining use of a rival, researching a rival on G2, rival named in job posts or on the stack, rival pricing and careers changes (HG Insights, G2 Buyer Intent, Verid, Apollo, PredictLeads, BuiltWith)

why_it_exists: A new executive, or a champion's move, is a reason to reach a person now.
processing: Champion changes job, new executive hire, buyer role change (Apollo Job Change Alerts, UserGems, PredictLeads). A champion move removes the signal tied to the old role and creates a new one at the new company

why_it_exists: How accounts engage with us (website, content, email) shows interest.
input: Web analytics and marketing automation events
processing: Visited our website (GA4, RB2B-style de-anonymisation), account researching us on G2, content download, email open or click. Pushed events are reconciled against the target list; unmatched events are discarded
output: First-party signals tied to an account
if_it_fails: Connector down: events queue and replay

why_it_exists: Replies, LinkedIn threads and call notes contain dates and next steps.
input: Replies, LinkedIn threads, calls and notes
processing: Replies on active threads; LinkedIn conversations (Dripify export, Sales Navigator); transcripts (renewal dates, requested follow-ups, budget statements)
output: Signals with next steps and expiry

why_it_exists: CRM activity shows a known contact resurfacing or a new contact appearing.
processing: A known contact resurfaces at a target account; an existing account now has a different contact

why_it_exists: A personal connection makes outreach warmer and more likely to work.
input: The team's LinkedIn connections (each rep's own login, own connections only, no bulk scrape); CRM relationships
processing: Map connections to target contacts; a personal connection is a reason to act now

why_it_exists: Buyers now research through AI assistants, and that traffic is intent.
input: Referral traffic from AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude)
processing: Match referrers and sessions to accounts and raise a first-party signal

why_it_exists: A late or repeated signal should weigh less than a fresh first one.
processing: Checked once for this signal. Recency: age when it enters, not when processed. Frequency: whether the same signal type has recurred for this account. Same event reported by several sources is merged. A stale or fifth-repeat signal weighs less

why_it_exists: Only signals that are verifiable, predictive and time-bound should count.
processing: Must pass all three tests or it is discarded. Observable: verifiable from a public source. Predictive: a documented link to buying in this category. Time-bound: a finite relevance window
output: A qualified signal, or a discard with the failed test

why_it_exists: Two events of the same type are not equally strong. The content decides.
processing: An LLM reads what the signal actually says (the announcement, the post, the comment) and scores how strong and how relevant it is; two funding announcements are not automatically equal
output: A strength score and a relevance note

why_it_exists: Signals fade at different speeds. The tier sets the points and the decay.
processing: Signal tier 1: 100 points, full weight 48 to 72 hours, steep decay, near zero by day 7 to 14. Signal tier 2: 60 points, full weight 1 to 2 weeks, fades over 30 to 60 days. Signal tier 3: 30 points, slow window 60 to 90 days
output: A tier, a decay curve and an expiry

why_it_exists: A signal that no longer applies (a champion moved) must be removed, and each signal tied to the right persona.
processing: Remove or replace signals made obsolete (a champion's job change); map each signal to the persona it concerns; keep the source

why_it_exists: Some signals (a positive reply, a live demo) need action in minutes, not the next morning.
input: A positive reply on an active thread, live webinar or demo attendance, a high-confidence comment on a post the account owns
processing: Skips the standard cycle and goes to NBA within minutes
output: An alert and an action within minutes

why_it_exists: A signal far outside its normal range may be a real event worth an alert.
input: A signal far outside its own statistical range
processing: Range per signal type, not a fixed number. Temporary signal tier 1 override for every account behind it, a real-time alert to the assigned rep, and the event goes to continuous discovery. Not smoothed back to the average

why_it_exists: New signals should earn weight from results, and sources that fail should be flagged.
input: Outcomes with the source that produced the signal
processing: New signal types start at zero weight and earn it from results. Sources whose signals convert are weighted up; sources that consistently fail are flagged for a vendor-renewal review

why_it_exists: The list of signals must keep growing as gaps and anomalies appear.
processing: Research keeps looking for new signal types and sources so the taxonomy does not go stale

why_it_exists: Comments, likes and shares on LinkedIn show interest, but only if the content shows the interest is relevant.
input: Comments, likes and shares by contacts at target accounts on LinkedIn posts: the customer's own company page and rep posts, and posts by the account, from licensed engagement providers
processing: Capture who engaged, how (comment, share, like) and on which post. Content in context: the AI reads the post and the comment text and judges whether it is relevant to the category, what the person meant (a question, an opinion, a share with a comment, a passive like) and how senior they are, then sets the strength. A like on an unrelated post is discarded at the qualification filter; a comment asking a question on a relevant post is strong. Proposed signal tiers: comment 2, share with a comment 2, share 3, like 3
output: Dated, sourced engagement signals with a relevance judgement
in_r1: Comment, share and like with content in context; source per PD27
in_r2: Fast lane for a high-confidence comment (SIG-17)
if_it_fails: Source not licensed: seeded and labelled; relevance unclear: strength 2, flagged

why_it_exists: Reps need to know how well an account matches the ICP.
input: Account attributes; ICP criteria and weights
processing: Weighted ICP match, 0 to 100, in code
if_it_fails: Missing attributes: held unranked, never a default fit

why_it_exists: Timing must reflect how many live signals there are, and how fresh and strong they are.
processing: Order strongest to weakest: Timing = S1 + 0.5 x S2 + 0.25 x S3 + 0.125 x S4 and so on. No cap; the total converges so one strong signal outweighs a pile of weak ones

why_it_exists: Ranking by fit times timing puts accounts that fit and are ready first. A good fit with nothing happening ranks zero.
processing: Rank = Fit x Timing (multiplied, so a perfect fit with no live signal ranks zero); account tier A, B, C by cut-off; disqualifiers subtract

why_it_exists: A rank needs a one-line reason and an honest confidence.
processing: A one-line reason from the stack and a confidence flag from identity, sources, strength and evidence
output: A why line and a confidence value
if_it_fails: LLM down: template from the top two signals

why_it_exists: Scoring must be proven on known won and lost accounts before reps rely on it.
processing: Run blind; pass bar in section 9; dry run on one rep's list
output: Pass or fix before go live
if_it_fails: Below 9 of 15 won: sell research, not scoring

why_it_exists: Scoring rules should be drafted from the customer's own won deals and be readable.
processing: AI drafts readable scoring rules from won deals; spread and spot checks first; a person reviews

why_it_exists: Big accounts always have signals, so each account should be compared with its own normal.
processing: Each account compared with its own normal, so big accounts do not dominate

why_it_exists: Weights should be re-learned from outcomes.
processing: Monthly re-weigh of tiers and weights against outcomes, behind the backtest gate

why_it_exists: Messages and plays must fit the customer's niche, not only the industry.
processing: Classify below industry (plant or process type) against a fixed taxonomy with a confidence
if_it_fails: Low confidence: unclassified, to the rep

why_it_exists: What triggered the account decides the angle of the message.
processing: Niche x trigger (funding, exec hire, compliance deadline, breach, tech-stack, M&A), a first pass treated as a thesis

why_it_exists: The message depends on who is being contacted.
processing: Title rules, LLM as fallback: buyer, technical lead, operations, procurement

why_it_exists: Nothing may be routed to an excluded account, or one touched recently.
processing: Customers, open deals, competitors, partners, paused segments and recent touches checked before routing

why_it_exists: Selling to a committee needs the right set of people.
processing: Committee per account: buyer, technical lead, operations

why_it_exists: The framing depends on whether buyers care about growth or cost.
processing: Text mining classifies why buyers bought: growth-framed or cost-framed. Sets message framing only, never rank

why_it_exists: A group sharing a trigger is best worked as one campaign. A rule decides when.
processing: The rule that decides NBA or NBC: when 10 or more accounts land in the same microsegment within a rolling 7 days (default) the segment is flagged for a campaign; below that each account gets an NBA

why_it_exists: What worked per segment should shape the next plays.
processing: What worked per segment

why_it_exists: Two reps must not work the same live opportunity, and history must inform the message.
processing: Gate: active owner or open opportunity holds the account and nothing downstream runs. History (every prior call, email, meeting and outcome) always passes forward as context
output: Blocked or cleared account with history

why_it_exists: A warm path changes the channel and the odds.
processing: Weighted score from connection count, seniority and strength, plus whether an internal relationship exists
output: A score for routing and channel

why_it_exists: Reps need to know the moment someone else engages, an account closes or a champion moves.
processing: Watches for engagement by someone else, a closed-won or a champion role change and tells the rep the moment it happens

why_it_exists: Messages need a proven structure. Until one is proven, the draft is marked unproven.
processing: The AI writes every message. The cache stores structure (angle, elements, order), never text. Validated structure: write against it. No validated structure: provisional, flagged unproven, to the rep. Explore: a deliberately different structure
output: A message structure and its status

why_it_exists: A rep needs one decided action: who, what, channel, why now, with the evidence.
input: Score, signals and evidence, contact, segment, history, motivation tag, category research
processing: Who, what, channel, why now, the draft, signals cited, and one format (plain text by default; PPT, doc, infographic, video, podcast, landing page or carousel when the trigger warrants it)
if_it_fails: LLM fails: no draft, to the rep with signals attached

why_it_exists: The channel should be chosen from verified data and from what has worked.
input: Verified contact data, warm-path strength, signal urgency, history
processing: Choose email, LinkedIn or phone; do not repeat a channel that failed on this account
if_it_fails: No verified channel: to the rep

why_it_exists: Nothing unsupported or off-brand should go out.
processing: Claims must match an approved claim or cite evidence; tone and style rules; banned phrases; a second AI checks facts and tone
output: A verified draft or a flagged one
if_it_fails: Unsupported claim: removed, or to the rep

why_it_exists: The AI should decide what it can and give a person only what it cannot.
input: Confidence; verification result; protective checks; identity tier; autonomy policy
processing: The AI proceeds on its own only when all five hold: confidence is high; message verification passes; every protective check passes; identity tier is I1 or I2; the segment's autonomy policy allows it. Any item that fails a criterion becomes an approval card for the owning rep. Low confidence goes to nurture. A campaign (NBC) always goes to the sales manager
in_r1: Criteria and routing; assisted mode by default

why_it_exists: A person decides the items that fail a criterion, and every campaign.
input: A routed action that failed a criterion, or an NBC
processing: Shown only for an item that failed a criterion or needs a human decision, and for every NBC. The rep (or manager for an NBC) approves, edits or skips; edits are stored as diffs; the decision is logged. An item that meets every criterion never gets a card
if_it_fails: No action in 3 days (default): expire and re-rank

why_it_exists: Reps start the day with a ranked list of what changed and what to do.
input: Tier A and B accounts; overnight changes
processing: Built at 6am per rep: what changed, with a drafted action, in chat
if_it_fails: Build fails: yesterday's queue marked "as of"

why_it_exists: A trigger shared by many accounts is worth one coordinated three-touch campaign.
input: Campaign flag (SEG-07); the accounts in the segment and their signals
processing: At the start of this stage the rule decides NBA or NBC. For an NBC the AI builds a three-touch sequence, each touch with its own message, channel and timing: day 0 plain text referencing the shared trigger; day 3 to 5 a message that reinforces the angle and cites an existing asset or statistic from the Knowledge Hub; day 7 to 10 a direct ask referencing both. The sales manager must confirm the campaign before it starts, always. Touches go to each account owner as scheduled tasks; a logged reply removes that account's pending touches. Before each touch the protective checks and message verification run again; a failure holds that touch and escalates it to the owning rep
output: A confirmed sequence for the segment
in_r1: Detection; three text touches; channel and timing per touch; manager confirmation; tasks per rep; stop on a logged reply
in_r2: Generated assets per touch; format confirmation per touch; plays
if_it_fails: No answer in 3 days: fall back to individual NBAs

why_it_exists: Repeatable outreach needs versioned plays.
processing: Trigger, qualifier, persona, steps, asset; fixed steps kept apart from AI steps; tiers auto, review, nurture; versioned

why_it_exists: The list must re-order the moment something happens.
processing: The queue re-orders the moment something happens

why_it_exists: Work must go to the right team by territory, product or deal size.
processing: Route to a team, not only a person

why_it_exists: Actions must reach reps where they work.
processing: Recommendation to the rep in chat, in Slack or Teams, or through MCP. "Sent, no response yet" is a real notification

why_it_exists: The system should reuse what is proven and keep testing alternatives.
processing: Validated pattern: 10 or more outcomes and confidence (successes + 1) / (attempts + 2) of 0.6 or more; demoted if the trailing 90-day rate drops below the threshold; trust decays with time since last confirmed use (threshold undefined). A small share of messages tests a different structure. A segment that stops converting routes back to explore

why_it_exists: Writers and checkers need one source of voice, tone, approved claims and banned phrases.
input: Voice and tone guide, brand guidelines, approved claims, banned phrases, templates, examples of bad drafts
processing: Structured store inside the Knowledge Hub: approved claims carry a source and a review date; banned phrases are enforced in verification; style rules come from bad examples
output: Rules the writer and the verifier use
in_r1: Store; enforced in NBA message verification

why_it_exists: Assets (decks, one-pagers) must be made in the customer's brand without us building a design tool.
input: A brief asking for an asset
processing: A headless engine produces the asset from the client's brand template. Plug-in candidates: Claude (text and design), Canva Connect and MCP, Moda, Figma MCP, Gamma; video HeyGen or Synthesia (R3). To evaluate for API access, brand templates and cost

why_it_exists: Different steps need different formats.
processing: Email, LinkedIn message, LinkedIn post (text), single image post, carousel (PDF slides), one-pager PDF, brochure, infographic, PPT deck (pitch or demo), case study, ROI sheet. Later: short video, podcast, landing page
in_r2: One-pagers, case studies, decks, carousels, single images

why_it_exists: Assets must be grounded, cited and checked before use.
processing: Grounded in the Knowledge Hub by retrieval; a second AI checks facts, tone and style; approved claims enforced; approval card; versioned
if_it_fails: Verification fails: regenerate once, then to the rep

why_it_exists: Outreach should open with why the account fits, and cite sources.
processing: Drafts open with why it fits, who to contact and numbered sources

why_it_exists: Past campaigns should become experience for the next one.
processing: Store each campaign: structure, segment, signal, persona, channel, message version, result. New briefs start from what worked for similar accounts. Past campaigns become experience

why_it_exists: Questions the library cannot answer show what content is missing.
input: Questions the library could not answer
processing: Log, cluster, rank; becomes the content backlog for the client

why_it_exists: An asset should be swappable in a live campaign.
processing: One asset per play step and persona; swappable in a live campaign
if_it_fails: Missing asset: step sends without one

why_it_exists: Rep edits show what good looks like, so the system should learn from them.
processing: Edits and results train a reward model; the best of several drafts goes first

why_it_exists: Repeated narrow jobs should run on small, cheap models.
processing: Fast, cheap models for narrow, repeated work; code for fixed steps
if_it_fails: Falls back to the general model

feature: Interim sending via the rep's mailbox
why_it_exists: Until integrated sending exists, reps send from their own mailbox, and the system must still capture each send.
processing: The rep sends from their own mailbox (Outlook through Microsoft Graph, or Gmail); the send is read back and logged with write-time capture
if_it_fails: Read-back fails: the rep logs it by hand

why_it_exists: The system must enforce who approves what, and when the AI may send alone.
processing: Assisted (the rep clicks send) or autopilot (the AI sends within guardrails). The system enforces whichever applies: a send is refused if its required approval is missing. Autopilot is enabled per segment only after the backtest and dry run

why_it_exists: A person must never be hit on three channels in 48 hours.
processing: Never three channels in 48 hours; respect send windows; check whether the same person is active or queued on another channel; coordinate or sequence a conflict

why_it_exists: Sends should run through the tools the customer already uses.
processing: Send through the client's tools: email sequencers, Dripify, Marketing Cloud, HubSpot sequences; pause on any reply or opt-out

why_it_exists: Customer teams should be able to run campaigns themselves by connecting their tools.
processing: Teams connect their own sending tools and run campaigns on their own; Demand AI decides and records

why_it_exists: Follow-up should continue until there is a clear answer.
input: A thread with no clear answer
processing: Keep following up until a clear answer, with stop on reply

why_it_exists: Every reply must be saved against its account.
input: Email and CRM feeds; send log
processing: Match each reply to its send and contact; log on the timeline; opt-outs added by the rep in R1

why_it_exists: Each reply needs a status and a default next step.
processing: A classifier assigns Hot (book the meeting), Further action (send the asset within a day), Not now (recontact date, nurture), Wrong person (add and re-route), Disqualified (close out, watch for renewal, save the reason as a lesson), Opted out (stop all, add to exclusions). Unsure replies go to the rep

why_it_exists: We must know which signal and message started each conversation.
processing: Account lineage from first touch; reply rate by signal type

why_it_exists: Someone who looked but did not reply is a warm lead.
processing: Message views (Dripify exports) and profile views (LinkedIn Premium or Sales Navigator), where available

why_it_exists: Which reply beat which objection should improve future replies.
processing: Which reply to which objection moved the deal, per segment

why_it_exists: Every decision must be logged, and today's numbers recorded as the baseline.
processing: Every decision logged; today's numbers recorded as the baseline

why_it_exists: Outcomes, hits and misses alike, are what the system learns from.
input: Meetings booked or not, with the microsegment, structure and channel used
processing: Log success and miss alike; both count in the confidence math

feature: Funnel per 100 and prioritised vs the rest
why_it_exists: Results must be compared fairly: per 100 accounts, and prioritised against the rest.
processing: Qualified to contacted to replied to meetings to won per 100 accounts worked; prioritised accounts against the rest, in the client's CRM, quarterly

why_it_exists: Rep, manager and leader each need their own numbers.
processing: Three views of the same data: sales rep (activity), sales manager (rates), sales leader (money); reply status mix, acceptance, edit rate, time to approve, cost per result, signal-to-reply by source

why_it_exists: The customer pays per qualified meeting, so the definition must be tracked.
processing: A held first meeting with a buying-committee persona at a Tier A or B account we surfaced, confirmed by the client's sales manager within five working days. Ours if the recommendation came before the first touch within 60 days and the trace is logged. Not billed: no-shows, existing customers, open opportunities, a second meeting at the same account in a quarter
output: A ledger and a quarterly true-up

why_it_exists: The system should improve every month without a bigger model.
processing: Monthly: graduate and demote patterns; decay trust; re-weigh tiers; score sources; coverage check (no signal on record = coverage gap; signal existed but scored low = calibration error). Gated by the backtest

why_it_exists: Each channel should be checked against an outside benchmark.
processing: Compare each channel with an external benchmark; flag below baseline directly

why_it_exists: A person should review learned changes before they ship.
processing: A person reviews changes weekly; nothing ships without the backtest

why_it_exists: A leader needs the gap to quota and a plan to close it.
input: Quota; closed deals; coverage; win rates
processing: Gap to quota and a week-by-week plan with named deals to push and accounts to open

why_it_exists: We need to know why customers in the category buy, and what they cite.
processing: Who buys this category, why, and what problem they cite; a reference set refreshed automatically; feeds fit weighting, objection handling and signal qualification

feature: Rival detection, review reading and matching
why_it_exists: What a rival's customers complain about is the angle for our message.
processing: Detect the rival (install data, CRM notes, job posts); read recent G2 reviews and cluster complaints; match each theme to our proof; the strongest theme becomes the angle; a renewal window makes it urgent. Start with public pages; check G2 terms

why_it_exists: Complaint themes should be tested against replies, per segment.
processing: Test themes against replies to learn which complaint moves buyers per segment

why_it_exists: The customer's own won conversations hold patterns worth mining.
processing: Suggested, not built: mine winning conversations for patterns

feature: Who replied, and what to write
why_it_exists: A rep's first question each morning is who replied and what to write.
processing: Sorts replies into six statuses, reads the thread and memory, drafts a grounded reply. You approve send, edit or skip; set recontact dates. Memory saves status, edits, outcome
output: Replies by status, Hot first, with drafts

feature: Who has not replied but looked
why_it_exists: Someone who looked but did not reply is worth a second touch.
processing: Segments replied, viewed message, viewed profile, no activity; ranks by fit and signals. Memory saves views with dates
output: Ranked warm non-responders with a next touch

why_it_exists: Managers and reps need to see which step of a campaign is weak and what to change.
processing: Per-100 results by step, persona and signal; reads stalled threads; audience or angle? You approve running a one-change test. Memory saves test, result, lesson
output: The weakest step, why, and a rewritten message

why_it_exists: A rep needs one account's whole history before a call.
processing: Builds the timeline: signals, actions, reasons, outcomes, buying committee. You approve the next step. Memory saves new signals, decision
output: First touch to today with the next step and source

why_it_exists: A meeting needs a brief, a deck and the missing stakeholders found.
processing: Reads profiles and threads for needs, finds missing stakeholders, builds a demo deck. You edit and approve. Memory saves needs, deck version, attendees
output: A brief, deck and one-pager per meeting

feature: Follow up on this week's demos
why_it_exists: After a demo the follow-up, gaps and risks must be captured the same day.
processing: Turns notes into next steps, finds qualification gaps, drafts a recap and PDF. You send and book the next meeting. Memory saves next steps, gaps, risk
output: Next steps, gaps, risk flag, recap

feature: How far am I from quota
why_it_exists: A rep needs to know how far they are from quota and what to do about it.
processing: Closed against quota, coverage, win rates; ranks deals to push and accounts to open. You accept or adjust. Memory saves plan, progress, outcomes
output: The gap and a weekly plan

why_it_exists: The customer's CRM stays the record. We read it so we never contact customers or open deals, and we never write to it.
processing: Salesforce (primary), HubSpot, Dynamics 365. Read-only: Demand AI never writes to the customer's CRM. Reads accounts, contacts, deals, stages, activity and the closed-won field
if_it_fails: CRM down: last snapshot; checks that need the CRM hold

why_it_exists: Sends, replies and meetings live in email and calendar.
input: Microsoft Graph (Outlook); Gmail and Google Calendar
processing: Read sends, replies and meetings; send as the rep

why_it_exists: Reps work in Slack and need alerts and actions there.
processing: Push notifications of actions and alerts (R1); interactive approval cards and queries (R2)

why_it_exists: Reps work in Teams and need alerts and actions there.
processing: Same as Slack; also captures inquiries as signals

why_it_exists: Power users and operations want a command line.
processing: Ask, queue, approve, status and admin commands for power users and operations

why_it_exists: The customer's own tools and other agents should be able to call our reasoning layer.
processing: Exposes the reasoning layer (queue, why, brief, memory) to Claude, OpenAI-based agents or the customer's own tooling

why_it_exists: Our agents should be able to use the tools the customer has already connected.
input: HubSpot MCP and other MCP servers
processing: Consume the customer's connected MCP servers (HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack and others)

why_it_exists: First-party events (web, marketing) are signals.
input: GA4, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Salesforce Marketing Cloud
processing: Bring first-party events into signals; enable nurture sends

why_it_exists: Conversations and LinkedIn views are signals.
input: Transcript sources (Gong, Fireflies, Teams), Dripify, Sales Navigator
processing: Bring conversations and views into signals

why_it_exists: Customers want the data in their own BI tools.
processing: Power BI export; open API; webhooks
